title: Metadata tied to particular timestamps
statement: As a bioimage analyst,\nI want to save metadata tied to particular timestamps,\nso we can correctly process data acquired in non-uniform sampling protocols, used in e.g. long time lapses and smart microscopy setups.
workaround: RFC-5 coordinate transform mapping frames to acquisition time
notes: 0.5: No coordinates transform in 0.5; frame times and events need custom attributes.\n0.6: Awkward: Frame-to-time mapping fits a `coordinates` transformation, but its array must be a valid multiscale image with 2 or 3 space axes, so a plain 1D time lookup is not allowed; it needs dummy spatial axes. Arbitrary metadata tied to timepoints (events) has no place in the spec.\n0.9dev: Suggestion: timestamps work as in STORY-002 (Possible), but event metadata still has no place.

title: Timestamps for non-uniform temporal sampling
statement: As an image analyst working with live-imaging data I encounter data that is non-uniformly sampled in time. This could be due to interruptions in long-term acquisitions or experimentally preferred variable sampling rates (e.g., lower sampling rate early on when a sample is more susceptible to photo-toxicity, event based changes to sampling rate in a smart microscopy setting). I want to store per-frame timestamps that allow correct visualization and processing (e.g., velocity estimation) of the data. The example stores POSIX timestamps as a parquet table, or as an array in the DCA metadata. In OME-Zarr v0.6 an alternative would be to use a RFC-5 coordinates transform.
workaround: RFC-5 coordinates (time array); else parquet table or custom attributes
notes: 0.5: Time can only be scaled uniformly (scale/translation); per-frame timestamps need custom attributes.\n0.6: Awkward: Same as STORY-001: per-frame timestamps can be a `coordinates` transformation on the time axis, padded with spatial axes to satisfy the multiscale constraints. Workable, but nothing is dedicated to it.\n0.9dev: Suggestion: RFC-3 lifts the 2–3 space axes rule, so a 1D `coordinates` lookup on t works without dummy axes; looks Possible rather than Unsure.

title: Some channels only imaged at certain time points
statement: As a bioimage analyst in a microscopy core facility, I came across the following problem: I want to convert time lapse data generated by a high-content screening microscope to ome-zarr. The problem is that some channels are acquired at all time points, while other channels are only acquired at some time points. This is to reduce the amount of acquired data, as not all channels are needed for time-dependent analysis. The question is now how best to save this into ome-zarr. Should all channels be saved into one zarr-array with the missing time-points / channels as zeros? Or should the channels be saved in separate arrays and connected with appropriate transforms?
notes: 0.5: No scene: channel groups can be separate entries in the `multiscales` list (or bioformats2raw series), each with its own axes, but nothing relates them.\n0.6: Store the channel groups as separate images, each with its own time axis and scale, related in a `scene`. One image with sparse channels is not possible: every channel shares the same time axis.\n0.9dev: As 0.6: separate images in a `scene`, each with its own time axis.

title: Some channels as z-stacks, others as single planes
statement: As a bioimage analyst in a microscopy core facility, I came across the following problem: I want to convert data generated by a high-content screening microscope to ome-zarr. The problem is that for some channels the entire z-stack is saved, while for other channels only a single 2D image is saved. They can either be a single z-slice, or a projected image. This is to reduce the amount of acquired data, as not all channels are needed for 3D analysis. The question is now how best to save this into ome-zarr. Should all channels be saved into one zarr-array with the missing z-slices / channels as zeros? Or should the channels be saved in separate arrays and connected with appropriate transforms? Usually the same metadata will apply to the 2D image as the z-stack. Is there a place to write this once and reference across the two zarr files? Is this solved by collections/RFC-8?
notes: 0.5: No scene or projectAxis: the 2D channels can be stored as a separate 3D image with one z plane, but linking it to the 3D image is implicit.\n0.6: Store the 3D and 2D channels as separate images in a `scene`; `projectAxis` (createdOutputs) places the 2D image in the 3D space. Metadata shared by both images cannot be written once: there is no shared or collection-level metadata.\n0.9dev: As 0.6: separate images in a `scene`, `projectAxis` places the 2D image.

title: Per-timepoint normalization statistics and annotations
statement: As a data scientist, I may want to pre-compute and store summary statistics at the dataset level or per timepoint when processing images. This is helpful so that I (or other downstream users) can later apply different types of data normalization approaches efficiently without reading full images. It’s also possible there might be other timepoint annotations, such as timestamps or the timepoint of an ablation or intervention, that I want to save. There isn’t a convention for how to store these timepoint annotations or statistics in ome-zarr or other metadata that are indexed by timepoint. Where should these data be stored? If you have a lot of timepoints, this can make the zarr.json really large and overcrowd other metadata stored there. It could be saved in a tabular format as well or as an array. Also, how do we want to index time? Should we use frames or the origin timestamp + gap from the previous frame (relevant to the non-uniform temporal sampling story as well)? How does this impact downsampled arrays?
notes: 0.5: No tables or per-timepoint annotations.\n0.6: No tables and no per-timepoint annotations in 0.6; only custom attributes or side files.\n0.9dev: No tables or per-timepoint annotations.

title: Biological annotations for channels
statement: As a data scientist, I would like to index and record the type of channel and relevant biology in a dataset. While most processing pipelines assume a fixed, ordered set of channels, this breaks down across a large repository of data. For some channel types (i.e. fluorescence), it’s helpful to include target, marker, labeled structures, labeled molecules, or marker type. For other channel types (i.e. label-free), simple free-text descriptions could work. How does the community want to reference and look up biological relevant annotations (i.e. by name or index)? What is the core model that’s relevant for all channels? In an HCS plate, this information may be duplicated many times within a zarr. Where is this information stored? Is there a way to only reference it once?
workaround: DCA channel-metadata spec
notes: 0.5: Only `omero` channel `label`; the rest is custom.\n0.6: Only the transitional `omero` channel `label` exists; target, marker and structure need custom attributes. No way to declare it once per plate.\n0.9dev: Only `omero` channel `label`.

title: Linear intensity calibration
statement: As a bioimage analyst in a microscopy core facility,\nI want to have calibrated intensity values of my images. I would like to apply different corrections, like subtraction of a constant background value, and linear scaling of intensities. One example would be, that we want to compensate for varying instrument sensitivity over long periods of time. We can track the instrument performance with reference measurements and then correct the images accordingly. Burning these corrections into the data has several downsides, like duplication / alteration of data, or reduction in intensity resolution (when rounding floats to integers). Therefore, it would be great, if these intensity calibrations could be described in the spec somewhere.
notes: 0.5: No intensity transformations.\n0.6: No intensity transformations in the spec. `omero` `coefficient`/`family` are display settings only.\n0.9dev: No intensity transformations.

title: Nonlinear intensity calibration
statement: As a bioimage analyst in a microscopy core facility,\nI want to have calibrated intensity values of my images. For example, a detector can have a non-linear response to the incoming light intensity, i.e. it is less efficient at high photon count rates. If I have a calibration curve of the detector, I can account for this. Burning these corrections into the data has several downsides, like duplication / alteration of data, or reduction in intensity resolution (when rounding floats to integers). Therefore, it would be great, if these intensity calibrations could be described in the spec somewhere.
notes: 0.5: No intensity transformations.\n0.6: No intensity transformations in the spec; a calibration curve needs custom attributes or an extra array.\n0.9dev: No intensity transformations.

title: Spatially varying intensity correction
statement: As a bioimage analyst in a microscopy core facility,\nI want to be able to account for inhomogeneous illumination. Microscopes often have inhomogeneous illumination across the field of view. One can account for this by dividing the image by a reference “flatfield” image. Burning these corrections into the data leads to duplication / alteration of the original data. Therefore, it would be great, if these corrections could be described in the spec somewhere.
notes: 0.5: No intensity correction.\n0.6: No intensity correction in the spec. The flatfield can be stored as another image, but linking it as a correction is custom.\n0.9dev: No intensity correction.

title: Metadata at different collection levels
statement: Related to biological DCA metadata, I might want to write some components associated with a set of movies (e.g., generated in one acquisition all containing the same biological specimen) and others with only a subset of them (e.g., perturbation conditions within an experiment).
notes: 0.5: Only plate, well and the transitional bioformats2raw layout; other collections are custom.\n0.6: 0.6 has no metadata for arbitrary collections (only plate, well, scene and the transitional bioformats2raw layout); anything else is custom attributes on a group.\n0.9dev: Only plate, well, scene and bioformats2raw; RFC-8 collections not in this draft.

title: Per-coordinate transforms along c and t
statement:
As an image analyst and microscopy pipeline developer,
I want to be able to apply different transforms to different coordinates along a non-spatial image dimension of an existing image,
so that I can save the transformations resulting from processing steps such as the following in OME-Zarr transformation metadata, avoiding the need for resampling of the image data: drift correction (one transformation per coordinate along dim t); channel alignment (one transformation per coordinate along dim c).

Note: RFC5 mentions the by-coordinate transformation in "future possibilities".
workaround: Resample data; RFC-5 lists by-coordinate transforms as future possibility
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms, applied to the whole array; no per-channel or per-timepoint transforms.\n0.6: Awkward: Along t: a `displacements` field indexed by time (with coarse spatial sampling) can hold one shift per timepoint, without resampling. Along c: not inside one image, since a transformation applies to the whole array; channels must be split into separate images in a `scene`, each with its own transform.\n0.9dev: As 0.6; RFC-3 removes the dummy-axis problem for fields, but per-channel transforms still need channels split into separate images.

title: Large-scale tile stitching
statement: As a method developer for stitching large scale tiles, I would want the following:\n1. extend the spec with additional transformation types, so that new registration methods (e.g. non-rigid or other models) can be represented without waiting for a core spec revision.\n2. alignment information to live separately from the image data, so that I can compare multiple alignment solutions and compare them.
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; alignments cannot be stored apart from the images.\n0.6: A `scene` can hold several alignments as transforms and coordinate systems, but it must live in the same Zarr hierarchy as the tiles; truly separate alignments come with RFC-8 collections. New transformation types are not supported: only the listed types are valid, so a non-rigid model outside them is custom (or approximated by a displacement field).\n0.9dev: Only the listed transformation types are valid. RFC-8 would add prefixed extension types (e.g. myorg:nonlinear) and collections that reference tiles by path.

title: Images with different Z-ranges in one dataset
statement:
As a bioimaging data repository developer,
I want to represent fluorescence and bright-field images acquired over different Z-ranges within a single OME-Zarr dataset while preserving their spatial alignment,
so that users can visualize and analyze both images together without treating them as separate datasets.

Background and current limitations: in the dataset, fluorescence images were acquired across Z-planes 0-50, while bright-field images were acquired only at Z-planes 22-30. OME-Zarr 0.5 does not provide a standardized way to represent these images with different Z-ranges as a single spatially aligned dataset.

Possible solutions: this use case can be addressed using Scenes in OME-Zarr 0.6, which allow images with different dimensions to be grouped while preserving their spatial relationships.
workaround: Scenes (RFC-5)
notes: 0.5: No scene, but separate images (e.g. bioformats2raw series) with their own scale and translation share an implicit physical space.\n0.6: `scene` groups images of different shapes and keeps them aligned.

title: Link segmentations to their source channels
statement: As a bioimage or medical image analyst,\nI want to store several segmentations of the same image (including overlapping ones and ones tied to specific image channels) together with my OME-Zarr image, and record what each one is and which channel it comes from,\nso that overlapping structures (e.g. nucleus and cell, organ and tumor) and channel-specific segmentations are kept without loss, and other people and tools can tell which segmentation belongs to which channel without guessing from names.
notes: 0.5: `image-label` `source` points to an image, not a channel.\n0.6: Several, overlapping label images are Core (`labels` group). `image-label` `source` points to an image but not to a channel, so which channel a label comes from needs a custom key.\n0.9dev: `image-label` `source` points to an image, not a channel.

title: Multiscale levels in different storages
statement: As a data provider hosting large images,\nI want the resolution levels of an image to be able to sit in different filesets or locations (e.g. full resolution in archive storage, smaller levels on a fast server),\nso that viewers can load previews quickly, and I can add or move resolution levels without copying or rewriting the whole image.
notes: 0.5: `datasets` paths are relative to the multiscales group.\n0.6: `datasets` paths are relative to the multiscales group, so all levels live in the same hierarchy; levels elsewhere would break the multiscales definition.\n0.9dev: `datasets` paths are relative to the multiscales group.

title: Segmentations stored separately from the image
statement:
As a bioimage analyst working with public images,
I want to save my segmentations in my own fileset and link them to the original image,
so that I can create and share labels without write access to the original data or copying large images, and viewers can show image and labels together.

Also included: the need for "viewers to overlay a source OME-Zarr and a separate annotation/labels OME-Zarr at display time" (Mandloi2309, ngff#78) and ngff#42.
notes: 0.5: Labels must sit in the image `labels` group; external links are custom.\n0.6: Label images must sit in the image's own `labels` group. A separate fileset can hold a valid OME-Zarr image, but linking it to the original is custom.\n0.9dev: Labels must sit in the image `labels` group.

title: Default color and contrast per channel
statement:
As a bioimage data producer sharing multi-channel images,
I want to save a display color and contrast limits (display range) for each channel with my data,
so that any viewer opens the image looking the way I intended, and users don’t have to adjust every channel by hand.

Note: covered by the omero transitional metadata in OME-Zarr 0.6.
workaround: omero transitional metadata
notes: 0.5: Core extension (transitional omero metadata): `color` and `window` start/end.\n0.6: Core extension (transitional omero metadata): `omero` channels `color` and `window` start/end.\n0.9dev: Core extension (was marked Transitional before the scale changed).

title: Channels shown by default
statement: As a user opening images with many channels (e.g. 50+ in multiplexed imaging), I want the data to say which channels are switched on when the image first opens, so that I start from a readable view instead of an overlay of every channel, and the same channels show up in every viewer.\n\nNote: covered by the omero transitional metadata in OME-Zarr 0.6.
workaround: omero transitional metadata
notes: 0.5: Core extension (transitional omero metadata): `active`.\n0.6: Core extension (transitional omero metadata): `omero` channels `active`.\n0.9dev: Core extension (was marked Transitional before the scale changed).

title: Intensity range for display controls
statement:
As a viewer developer,
I want to know the meaningful intensity range of each channel (e.g. the actual minimum and maximum pixel values), separate from the default contrast,
so that contrast sliders cover a useful range instead of the full data type range (e.g. 0–65535).

Note: covered by the omero transitional metadata in OME-Zarr 0.6.
workaround: omero transitional metadata
notes: 0.5: Core extension (transitional omero metadata): `window` min/max.\n0.6: Core extension (transitional omero metadata): `omero` channels `window` min/max, separate from start/end.\n0.9dev: Core extension (was marked Transitional before the scale changed).

title: Lookup tables (colormaps)
statement: As a scientist visualizing intensity data,\nI want to say which lookup table or colormap a channel should use, and whether it’s inverted,\nso that images that depend on a specific colormap (e.g. heatmaps, inverted EM) display correctly everywhere, without relying on one server or application.
notes: 0.5: Only `omero` `inverted` and single `color`; no lookup tables.\n0.6: Inversion is Transitional (`omero` `inverted`), and `color` gives a single-colour ramp, but there is no field for a lookup table or named colormap; that needs custom attributes.\n0.9dev: `omero` has `inverted` and `color` but no lookup tables.

title: OME-XML sidecar file
statement:
As a data steward converting proprietary file formats to OME-Zarr,
I want a standard way to store a metadata.ome.xml file accessible from my Multiscale or Collection,
so I can preserve at least as much vendor metadata as when converting to OME-TIFF.

Note: currently doable in 0.6 with the bioformats2raw.layout transitional metadata.
workaround: bioformats2raw.layout transitional metadata
notes: 0.5: Core extension (transitional bioformats2raw.layout metadata) with `OME/METADATA.ome.xml`.\n0.6: Core extension (transitional bioformats2raw.layout metadata): `bioformats2raw.layout` with `OME/METADATA.ome.xml`, but only for that layout, not for an arbitrary multiscale or collection.\n0.9dev: Core extension (was marked Transitional before the scale changed).

title: OME-XML metadata as standardized JSON
statement: As a maintainer of a tool that reads/writes OME-Zarr,\nI want a standard way to store the same metadata captured in a metadata.ome.xml file, but using only standardized fields in JSON (e.g. in zarr.json),\nso I can preserve the vendor metadata without needing to know how to write/read/validate OME-XML and XML in general.
notes: 0.5: No standard JSON for OME-XML.\n0.6: No standard JSON for OME-XML metadata in 0.6; only custom attributes.

title: Photobleaching (FRAP) metadata
statement: As a bioimage analyst doing FRAP microscopy,\nI want to record the metadata for when the bleaching of the signal at a particular time with a lightsource. The properties of the photobleaching pulse (at least when and where it occurs) are relevant bits of metadata for this application. So I can seamlessly process the data in standardized workflows.
notes: 0.5: No acquisition or event metadata.\n0.6: No acquisition or event metadata in 0.6; custom attributes only.\n0.9dev: No acquisition or event metadata.

title: Basic axis names, units and scales
statement: 1. Microscope interfacing software reads data from microscope and writes in ome-zarr format. Axis names and units are hard coded while the scales are set based on the imaging parameters.\n2. User loads data in ImageJ/Neuroglancer and sees correct axis names and scale bars.
workaround: Feasible since 0.4 (axes + scale)
notes: 0.5: `axes` names, types, units and a `scale` per dataset.\n0.6: `axes` names, types and units plus a `scale` transform per dataset.

title: Prediction on a cutout aligned to the full volume
statement: 1. User runs CNN on cutout from existing volume in ome-zarr format and writes result as a new OME-Zarr volume, using a translation transformation to indicate the cutout location.\n2. User loads CNN output and original volume in ImageJ/Neuroglancer and sees output correctly aligned to original full-size volume.
workaround: Feasible since 0.4 (translation)
notes: 0.5: A `translation` places the cutout in the volume's physical space.\n0.6: A `translation` (in the dataset or `scene` transforms) places the cutout in the full volume.

title: Affine registration between two volumes
statement: 1. User runs affine registration between existing volumes A and B in ome-zarr format. After computing affine transform, software modifies metadata of volume B in place to indicate the affine transform.\n2. User loads data volumes A and B in Neuroglancer and sees them correctly aligned.
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; no affine.\n0.6: `affine` between the two images in a `scene`.

title: Non-rigid registration stored as a displacement field
statement: 1. User performs non-rigid registration between existing volumes A (a canonical atlas) and B in ome-zarr format. BigWarp updates transformation meta-data in volume B, the non-rigid transformation is stored as a displacement field in ome-zarr format.\n2. User loads data volumes A and B in BigDataViewer and sees them correctly aligned.\n3. User overlays segmentations performed on original volume B (Story 2) and sees them correctly aligned.
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; no displacement fields.\n0.6: `displacements` transformation; overlaying segmentations from B works through B's labels.

title: Registration of slices into a volume
statement: 1. User collects multiple overlapping/non-overlapping slices and stores each in ome-zarr format with appropriate transformations.\n2. User collates all slices into a single ome-zarr volume (registering neighboring slices, joining the data, or introducing zeros/nans as necessary)\n3. [Potential] User may want to simply save the transformations necessary to create the single volume on the fly.
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; slices needing rotation cannot be placed.\n0.6: Each slice as an image in a `scene` with its own transform. Collating them into one volume is up to tools, but the transforms are specified.

title: Stitching overlapping tiles
statement: Related to story 5\n1. User collects multiple overlapping 2d / 3d image tiles that are subsets of a whole.\n2. User performs stitching (e.g., with BigStitcher), and needs to track transforms from all tile spaces to world space.
notes: 0.5: Translation-only stitching: each tile a separate image with its own translation in an implicit shared space. Rotations or overlap refinement out of spec.\n0.6: One transform per tile to a shared coordinate system in a `scene`.

title: Lens correction applied to every 2D slice
statement: 1. User working with an imaging system estimates its lens distortion as a non-linear 2D transform and stores it with NGFF.\n2. User collects a 3D image.\n3. User applies the same lens correction transform to all 2d slices of the 3D image.
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; no displacements or byDimension.\n0.6: `byDimension`: a 2D `displacements` field on y and x, identity on z.

title: Multiscale pyramids in a shared physical space
statement:
1. User has a large image stored at high resolution.
2. User generates a multiscale pyramid by repeatedly downsampling and storing relevant metadata.
3. User opens the pyramid with a viewer that can interpret scales correctly, on-the-fly loading works properly.
   a. User can open two individual scales and can view them in the same physical space.
notes: 0.5: `multiscales` with scale (and translation) per level.\n0.6: `multiscales` with scale (and translation) per level in one intrinsic coordinate system.

title: Thickness of 2D slices
statement:
1. User collects 2d data with known / specified physical thickness.
2. User displays 2d slices in 3d with thickness displayed correctly.

Needs ability to apply M-dim transforms to N-dim data (M>N).
notes: 0.5: As 0.6: a 3D array with one z plane and z `scale` equal to the thickness.\n0.6: A 2D array has no axis to carry thickness. Storing it as a 3D array with one z plane and a z `scale` equal to the thickness works, since a voxel spans its full extent.\n0.9dev: Core extension (was marked Transitional before the scale changed).

title: Specialized metadata for different applications
statement: 1. User collects two datasets for ML training.\n2. Each has distinct coordinateTransform for display purposes (e.g. scale [4,4,3.8], scale [4,4,4.1])\n3. They share a coordinateTransform (e.g. scale [4,4,4]) to avoid interpolation when passing data to model.
notes: 0.5: Only one implicit physical coordinate system; no named extra coordinate systems.\n0.6: Extra coordinate systems with their own transforms in `multiscales` `coordinateTransformations`.

title: Reordering z-slices
statement: 1. User collects 2d images but they are written in an unpredictable order.\n2. After the fact, user writes the correct order of z-slices to transform metadata.\n3. A transformed view of the volume should display the slices in the correct order.
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; no slice lookup.\n0.6: Awkward: `mapAxis` permutes axes, not slices. Re-ordering needs a `coordinates` lookup on z (which the spec reserves for smooth fields) or each slice as its own image in a `scene`.

title: Stacking 2D images into a 3D image
statement: 1. User collects N 2d images each stored as its own array.\n2. User writes metadata to "stack" the 2d images along a third dimension using coordinateTransformations and a new coordinateSystem.\n3. Downstream software makes available a 3d image consisting of the N 2d images.
notes: 0.5: No projectAxis or scene: each 2D image stored as a one-plane 3D image with a z translation; only implicitly stacked.\n0.6: 2D images placed in a 3D coordinate system with `projectAxis` (createdOutputs) and a translation, in a `scene`.

title: Thin-plate spline transformations
statement: Similar to Story 4, but the thin-plate-spline parameters are stored in ome-zarr instead of the displacement field. That should save storage space and allow for transformations of annotations that are connected to the image but don't align to the voxel grid.
workaround: Displacement field (Story 4); RFC-5 author suggested waiting for a later revision, as it depends on storing points (landmarks)
notes: 0.5: No thin-plate splines.\n0.6: No thin-plate-spline type and no way to store landmarks; can only be approximated as a `displacements` field.\n0.9dev: No thin-plate splines; approximate as `displacements`.

title: Mesh-affine transformations
statement: Extends story 5 and 6. A section tile is divided in a triangle-mesh (i.e. non-overlapping triangles) and each triangle gets an affine transformation attached.\n\n(axtimwalde: storing the affines is not necessary; source and target coordinates of all vertices plus three vertex indices per triangle are enough and much more compact.)
workaround: RFC-5 author suggested waiting for a later revision, as it depends on storing points (mesh)
notes: 0.5: No mesh transforms.\n0.6: No mesh-based transform and no way to store meshes; can only be approximated as a `displacements` field.\n0.9dev: No mesh transforms; approximate as `displacements`.

title: Oblique plane microscopy: on-the-fly deskew
statement: 1. User collects skewed planes (OPM Snouty, Zeiss LLS7, diSPIM)\n2. Downstream software (BigDataViewer for instance) uses the skew transformation information (3d matrix for instance) to display the dataset in real physical space, without rasterisation of the dataset on an orthogonal XYZ array.
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; shear (affine) not allowed.\n0.6: A shear `affine` in `multiscales` `coordinateTransformations` deskews without resampling.

title: Stitching multi-angle acquisitions
statement:
Related to story 5 and 6
1. User collects multiple overlapping 2d / 3d image tiles that are subsets of a whole.
2. User repeats the operation 1. after having rotated significantly the sample (30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180, etc.)
3. User performs stitching (e.g., with BigStitcher), and needs to track transforms from all tile and all angle spaces to world space.
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; no rotation or affine.\n0.6: `rotation`/`affine` per tile and angle in a `scene`.

title: Registering multi-position acquisitions
statement:
1. User collects 3D volumes in multiple channels at multiple positions in a 96-well plate.
2. User analyzes the volumes to register the volumes in XYZ such that the focal plane is in the center of the volume.
3. User stores separate affine transformations for all positions.
4. User would like to view registered volume in napari/neuroglancer/ImageJ.
notes: 0.5: Stage positions as translations of separate images; rotation or affine correction is out of spec.\n0.6: One `affine` per position image in a `scene`.

title: Correspondence of histology to MRI coordinates
statement:
Related to 4, 5, 12 and 15, with details from the existing wb_view implementation
1. User collects T1w and other MRI scans of an animal, rigid aligns them and orients via ACPC or similar (not nonlinear or anisotropic affine)
2. Brain is extracted and sectioned, regularly spaced sections (whole brain, ~0.5mm in macaque) are stained, 2D scanned (and stitched) with full coverage (high resolution, image pyramids), with hemispheres and temporal pole pieces as separate images (due to FoV limits, separated tissue not being placed in correct relative position on the slide, bent corpus callosum misaligning hemispheres, etc)
3. Histology images are registered to MRI reference space, with the transform split into distinct parts.
   a. 2D to 2D affine for each piece to roughly position it within the section plane (for display without applying a deformation to image data)
   b. 2D to 2D deformation field (and its inverse) for each section to get accurate correspondence of histology tissue to the MRI tissue intersecting the section plane (tissue pliability, tearing, etc)
   c. 2D to 3D transform for each section to define the section plane in MRI mm space (currently affine, might include curvature in the future to deal with tissue deformation before sectioning)
4. For each image, a "distance beyond tissue edge" measurement is created for the tissue that the image is "responsible for", stored in rough aligned section plane space, used to resolve overlaps with background and/or clipped tissue when displaying all images from a section together.
5. User wants to display the histology image data one section at a time (all pieces in the section shown as per rough alignment), next to MRI data, and clicking on the histology moves the MRI display to the corresponding coordinate (and vice versa).
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; no affine, displacements or 2D-to-3D mapping.\n0.6: 2D `affine`, `displacements` with an explicit inverse (`bijection`) and a 2D-to-3D `affine` are all in 0.6; the distance map can be another image.

title: Drift correction: one transform per timepoint
statement:
Motivates transformations that transform spatial coordinates (affine etc.) but depend on / differ for non-spatial coordinates (e.g. t and c)
1. User has a timelapse of a drifting sample.
2. User performs drift correction, obtaining one (linear) transformation per timepoint.
3. User wants to save / visualize the drift corrected timelapse without resampling / transforming the timelapse.
workaround: Resample data; RFC-5 lists by-coordinate transforms as future possibility
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms, fixed for the whole array; no per-timepoint transform.\n0.6: Awkward: As STORY-011: a `displacements` field indexed by time gives one shift per timepoint without resampling. Rigid or affine motion per timepoint has to be expanded into displacements.\n0.9dev: As 0.6: one shift per timepoint via a time-indexed `displacements` field; rigid/affine per timepoint must be expanded.

title: Registration / stitching / multi-view reconstruction of timelapses
statement: 1. User story fits into stories 5, 6, 16, 17.\n2. Typically, resulting registration parameters vary over time (e.g. because of stage positioning errors among others)\n3. User wants to save / visualize the registered / reconstructed image dataset without resampling / transforming the timelapse.
workaround: Resample data; RFC-5 lists by-coordinate transforms as future possibility
notes: 0.5: As STORY-042.\n0.6: Awkward: As STORY-042, per tile or view: time-varying registration only as displacement fields indexed by time.\n0.9dev: As STORY-042.
related: STORY-028; STORY-029; STORY-039; STORY-040; STORY-042; STORY-011

title: Chromatic correction: one transform per channel
statement: 1. User has an image dataset exhibiting chromatic misalignment.\n2. User performs chromatic correction obtaining one transformation per channel.\n3. User wants to save / visualize the channel aligned image without resampling / transforming the image.
workaround: Resample data; RFC-5 lists by-coordinate transforms as future possibility
notes: 0.5: No per-channel transform; channels could be split but no affine exists.\n0.6: Awkward: One transform per channel only by splitting channels into separate images in a `scene`, each with its own affine.\n0.9dev: As 0.6: per-channel transforms only by splitting channels into images in a `scene`.

title: Registration of multiplexed imaging rounds
statement:
Goal: creating multi-channel (3d or 2d) image from multiple rounds of staining/acquisition
1. Acquire multiple rounds of 3-channel images with various markers, e.g.
   a. first round: markers A, B, C.
   b. second round: markers A, D, E.
   c. third round: markers A, F, G.
2. Register a, b and c via the common marker (A, A', A''), with elastic/non-linear or linear transformation as needed.
3. Display/process the image as 7-channel image (CZYX) with channels A, B, C, D, E, F, G without re-saving the transformed pixel/voxel data.
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; rounds usually need affine registration.\n0.6: Each round as an image with its own transform in a `scene`. Showing them as one 7-channel image is not defined: channels can't be merged across images.

title: Stitching and registration of tiled, multiplexed imaging
statement:
Combination of Story 6 and Story 22
1. Collect multiple overlapping 2d / 3d image tiles that are subsets of a whole, with multiple rounds of imaging. Each round contains a common registration marker.
2. Align tiles within each round of imaging (stitching) as well as between rounds (registration) using a tool such as Ashlar. Only corrected tile transformations are stored.
3. Display/process combined image with all tiles and all channels without re-saving the original image data.

(This also requires illumination/shading correction to be applied in step 3, but this correction is an intensity transform rather than a spatial coordinate transform so is not really in scope here.)
notes: 0.5: As STORY-045.\n0.6: As STORY-045 with tiles: transforms are Core, but combining all tiles and rounds into one multi-channel image is up to tools.

title: Cropping: bounds on an axis
statement: Motivates bounded (projective) coordinate spaces; intended for a follow-up transform RFC, not expected to be implemented in RFC-5\n1. User generates an N-D image.\n2. User defines a lower and upper bound to an axis.
workaround: Not in RFC-5; intended for a follow-up transform RFC
notes: 0.5: No bounds on coordinate systems.\n0.6: Coordinate systems have no bounds in 0.6; a crop needs custom metadata or a copied sub-array with a translation.\n0.9dev: Coordinate systems have no bounds.

title: Kymographs
statement:
Motivates bounded (projective) coordinate spaces; intended for a follow-up transform RFC, not expected to be implemented in RFC-5
1. User has 2D+time data.
2. User defines a line in 2D space.
3. Displays/process to a 2D image of time-line coordinate space.
workaround: Not in RFC-5; intended for a follow-up transform RFC
notes: 0.5: No coordinates transform.\n0.6: Awkward: A `coordinates` field sampled along the line can map a (time, position-along-line) system into the image. Its array needs 2 space axes, so one dummy axis is required.\n0.9dev: RFC-3 drops the 2–3 space axes rule, so a `coordinates` field along the line needs no dummy axis.

title: Curvilinear tube projection
statement:
Motivates bounded (projective) coordinate spaces; intended for a follow-up transform RFC, not expected to be implemented in RFC-5
1. User generates 3D + channel data.
2. User defines a spline in 3D space.
3. Process to an axis-aligned bounded space transformed around the spline.
workaround: Not in RFC-5; intended for a follow-up transform RFC
notes: 0.5: No coordinates transform.\n0.6: A `coordinates` field sampled around the spline maps a straightened tube into the image. The spline itself can't be stored, only its sampled field.\n0.9dev: As 0.6: a sampled `coordinates` field; the spline itself is not stored.

title: Mesh projection / surface quantification
statement:
Motivates bounded (projective) coordinate spaces; intended for a follow-up transform RFC, not expected to be implemented in RFC-5
1. User has a 3D image.
2. User defines a 2D surface mesh in 3D space.
3. User gets image values at the mesh coordinates / projected to the mesh coordinates.
workaround: Not in RFC-5; intended for a follow-up transform RFC
notes: 0.5: No coordinates transform.\n0.6: A surface that can be parameterized on a 2D grid fits a `coordinates` field. Arbitrary meshes can't be stored.\n0.9dev: As 0.6: parameterizable surfaces as a `coordinates` field; arbitrary meshes not.

title: CMI experiment as a graph of warped datasets
statement:
A correlative multimodal imaging experiment often involves multiple (>2) 3D datasets. A graph can be built such as: datasets are nodes; warp functions between any two datasets are edges linking these two nodes. A warp function (edge) between any two datasets can be defined by a set of parameters defining the origin and target datasets (e.g. dataset name, voxel size in metric units, offset, scale, axis flips) and a list of the coordinates of paired landmarks between these datasets. In this way, all edges and nodes can be listed in tables. The list of landmarks and warp functions can be sourced from BigWarp (and stored alongside the warp graph). This approach allows combining multiple warps in sequence (warping data across connected nodes in the graph). This approach not only allows warping the datasets themselves, but also the annotations drawn on any dataset. Any feature drawn on any dataset can be then overlaid onto any of the connected datasets seamlessly. Advantages:
1. Version control: the warp graph can be managed through git.
2. Scalability: more complex CMI workflows can be robustly built and shared efficiently across collaborators, e.g. a correlative light - XRay - EM workflow with multiple X-ray CT datasets obtained at different trimming stages.
3. Accuracy: by warping the annotations, any analysis can take place in the originally acquired datasets (instead of segmenting the warped datasets, which may have incorporated interpolation noise)
4. Cost-efficiency: packaging a CMI experiment only requires a single version of the original datasets (data-heavy) and the warp table (data-light); no dataset duplicates are needed.

This system has already been incorporated into an NGFF OME-Zarr data ecosystem (WEBKNOSSOS) as warpAnnotations, which facilitates multiuser collaboration and releasing CMI experiments.
notes: 0.5: No scene or non-scale/translation warps.\n0.6: The graph of datasets and warps maps onto a `scene` with transforms between images, and warps can be displacement fields. The landmarks behind each warp have no place in the spec.

title: Annotating and training with reference crops
statement:
1. User runs annotation tools (e.g. micro-sam) to segment reference crops (one or multiple); a reference crop is the same as the cut-outs in previous stories.
2. User writes the resulting annotated reference crop(s) in a new OME-Zarr volume (following Story 2).
   a. An interesting use-case would be to do the above two steps for data on an OMERO server (and ensure that the user does not have to create a zero array locally to do step 2)
3. User wants to train models on segmented reference crops only.
notes: 0.5: The crop can be its own image with a `translation` into the full image's physical space (implicit; no scene). Not as a label image, which must match the image shape.\n0.6: The annotated crop can be its own image placed with a `translation` in a `scene`, so no zero-filled full-size array is needed. Label images under `labels` must match the image shape, so a crop is not a label image there.

title: Converting vendor formats with extra dimensions
statement: As a data producer, I want to convert vendor files with dimensions beyond TCZYX (Zeiss CZI phases H, illuminations I, views V; Leica LIF λ, rotations A, mosaic M) to OME-Zarr without interleaving them into one custom axis or splitting the image, so that the result stays manageable.
notes:
0.5: Awkward: at most one channel/custom axis; extra dimensions must be interleaved into it or split into several images.
0.6: Awkward: same as 0.5.
0.9dev: Core: RFC-3 removes limits on number, names, order and type of axes.
0.5: Breaking: axes limited to 2-5 with at most one channel/custom axis; extra vendor dimensions cannot be stored losslessly.
0.6: Breaking: axes limited to 2-5 with at most one channel/custom axis; extra vendor dimensions cannot be stored losslessly.
sources: https://ngff.openmicroscopy.org/rfc/3/ (Conversion of existing microscopy data formats)

title: Store axes in acquisition order
statement: As a data producer, I want to write arrays in the order they are acquired (e.g. TZCYX), so that I do not have to transpose large datasets before saving.
notes:
0.5: Possible: the Zarr v3 transpose codec stores data in another order while the array keeps TCZYX.
0.6: Possible: transpose codec, or `mapAxis`.
0.9dev: Core: RFC-3 allows any axis order with only scale and translation.
0.5: Breaking: axis order is fixed (time, channel/custom, space); storing acquisition order is invalid.
0.6: Breaking: axis order is fixed (time, channel/custom, space); storing acquisition order is invalid.

title: Fluorescence lifetime (FLIM) data
statement: As a researcher doing FLIM, I want to store the decay (microtime) axis alongside channel, time and space (e.g. CTUZYX, 6D), so that lifetimes can be explored and analysed without splitting the data or using bare Zarr.
notes:
0.5: Awkward: six dimensions are not allowed; the decay axis must take the custom slot (losing channels) or the image is split.
0.6: Awkward: same as 0.5.
0.9dev: Core: RFC-3 removes limits on number, names, order and type of axes.
0.5: Breaking: TCZYX plus a lifetime axis is 6D, beyond the 2-5 axis limit.
0.6: Breaking: TCZYX plus a lifetime axis is 6D, beyond the 2-5 axis limit.

title: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD)
statement: As a materials scientist, I want to store a 2D diffraction pattern (dx, dy) for every scan position (x, y) as a 4D array with four space axes, plus per-pixel crystal orientation (Euler angles or quaternions), so that inferred grain boundaries can be checked against the raw patterns.
notes:
0.5: Awkward: at most 3 space axes; the pattern must be flattened into a custom axis.
0.6: Awkward: same as 0.5.
0.9dev: Core: RFC-3 removes limits on number, names, order and type of axes.
0.5: Breaking: needs four spatial-like axes; at most 3 space axes allowed.
0.6: Breaking: needs four spatial-like axes; at most 3 space axes allowed.

title: Diffusion tensors per voxel (DTI)
statement: As a researcher, I want to store a diffusion tensor at each voxel, either as one component axis or as a 2-axis symmetric matrix, so that DTI results live alongside the images.
notes: 0.5: Possible as one custom axis of components; a 2-axis matrix is not allowed.\n0.6: same as 0.5.\n0.9dev: Core: RFC-3 removes limits on number, names, order and type of axes.

title: Fourier-space images
statement: As a bioimage analyst, I want to save images in spatial-frequency space (axes w, v, u), so that intermediate products of filtering or deconvolution can be reprocessed later.
notes:
0.5: Awkward: frequency axes must be declared as space axes (or use the single custom slot).
0.6: same as 0.5.
0.9dev: Core: RFC-3 allows them and recommends the names w, v, u.
0.5: Breaking: space axes need spatial units; reciprocal (frequency) units are not allowed.
0.6: Breaking: space axes need spatial units; reciprocal (frequency) units are not allowed.

title: Overlapping or hierarchical labels
statement: As a bioimage analyst, I want to store overlapping instance masks or coarse-to-fine segmentations (tissue, cell, organelle) along an extra instance or coarseness axis, so that they can live as labels of the source image.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: label dimensions must match the image (or be 1); an extra axis is not allowed.\n0.6: same as 0.5 (several label images is the workaround).\n0.9dev: Possible: RFC-3 allows the extra axis, but labels are still described as matching the image dimensions; nothing dedicated to instance axes.

title: Computational outputs with arbitrary axes
statement: As a data scientist, I want to store outputs with extra axes (one per parameter of a grid search, original vs augmented instances for deep learning), so that they stay in OME-Zarr with metadata linking back to the raw data.
notes:
0.5: Awkward: only one custom axis; others must be split or interleaved.
0.6: same as 0.5.
0.9dev: Core: RFC-3 removes limits on number, names, order and type of axes.
0.5: Breaking: axes limited to 2-5 in a fixed order; arbitrary axes are invalid.
0.6: Breaking: axes limited to 2-5 in a fixed order; arbitrary axes are invalid.

title: Anatomical orientation of axes
statement: As a researcher aligning data to anatomical atlases, I want to record which anatomical direction each spatial axis runs (e.g. anterior-to-posterior), so that tools do not have to guess orientation, which is impossible for symmetric structures like the brain.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: custom attributes only.\n0.6: Out of spec: same as 0.5.\n0.9dev: Core: axis `orientation` with `type: anatomical` (RFC-4). For axes not aligned with anatomy, RFC-5 transforms to an anatomical coordinate system.

title: Subject-local orientation of tissue specimens
statement: As a researcher in spatial transcriptomics or histopathology, I want to record the orientation of a tissue specimen itself (e.g. superficial-to-deep in a skin biopsy, apical-to-basal in an epithelium) even when its place in the donor is unknown, so that it can be analysed without registering to a whole-body atlas.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: custom attributes only.\n0.6: Out of spec: same as 0.5.\n0.9dev: Core: RFC-4 subject-local values (superficial/deep, apical/basal, apex/base). Only one primary orientation per axis.

title: Standalone label images
statement: As a bioimage analyst or data manager,\nI want to store a label image (segmentation) as its own OME-Zarr fileset, without a parent intensity image or a labels/ group,\nso that segmentations can be shared and loaded on their own, as already done in practice (e.g. BIA AI-ready studies).
user_classes: Bioimage analyst; Data manager; Tool developer
workaround: Write a multiscales group at the root with the image-label key; readers that only check multiscales open it as a plain image.
notes: 0.5: Possible: a multiscales group with image-label works and is used, but the spec only describes labels nested under an image's labels/ group, so it is not clearly allowed.\n0.6: Possible: same; a scene can also hold the image and its label side by side, with image-label marking the label.\n0.9dev: Possible: unchanged; done when the text says a single image with image-label is valid. A labels RFC is expected.
sources: https://github.com/ome/ngff/issues/179 duplicate; https://github.com/ome/ngff/issues/536 labels epic; https://forum.image.sc/t/ome-zarr-hackathon-how-to-represent-labels/123114/9 labels RFC discussion; https://github.com/ome/ngff/issues/339; https://github.com/ome/ngff/issues/338

title: Several images shown together in one view
statement: As a researcher using viewers such as WEBKNOSSOS, Neuroglancer, MoBIE or OMERO.figure,\nI want to describe several images that map to a common space as one entity,\nso that I can share one link instead of many and every viewer opens the same set.
workaround: Viewer-specific JSON (MoBIE projects, Neuroglancer state) listing the images.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no way to group images; viewer-specific JSON only.\n0.6: Core: an RFC-5 scene groups images in shared coordinate systems. Rendering settings are a separate story.\n0.9dev: Core: same; RFC-8 would generalise scenes into collections.

title: Segmentations and prediction maps related to several images
statement: As a bioimage analyst,\nI want a label image or prediction map to refer to several images (m:n), e.g. correlated images of the same feature or channels stored as separate images,\nso that derived images are not tied to a single parent.
workaround: Duplicate the labels under each image, or record the links in custom attributes.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: labels are 1:n under one image; prediction maps have no defined kind.\n0.6: Out of spec: same; a scene can place them side by side but not say which image a label belongs to.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: not in 0.9dev; RFC-8 collections would cover it.

title: Workflow outputs that link to unchanged inputs
statement: As a tool developer of a workflow engine (Fractal, Voxelytics, Nextflow),\nI want a task to write its output (e.g. a prediction map) in a new fileset that links to the input image without copying it,\nso that inputs stay untouched and each task's output can be viewed with its input.
workaround: Copy the input, or write into the input fileset, or record the path in custom attributes.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no links to images outside the fileset.\n0.6: Out of spec: scenes reference images inside their own hierarchy only.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: not in 0.9dev; RFC-8 collections would cover it.

title: Flexible metadata for plates and wells
statement: As a data producer of high content screens,\nI want to say how images in a well relate (field of view, re-acquisition, processed result), and describe wells of different sizes or positions,\nso that viewers pick sensible defaults and plates can hold processing intermediates.
workaround: Custom attributes on the plate or well group.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: the HCS plate/well metadata has a fixed set of fields.\n0.6: Out of spec: same.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: not in 0.9dev; RFC-8 collections would cover it.

title: Image collections for archive deposition and access
statement: As a data manager at an image archive,\nI want submitters to group images and say how they relate (same acquisition series, plate/well), and to publish groupings that viewers understand,\nso that submissions can be parsed into records and data opens in many tools without a schema per tool.
workaround: Plates for HCS; otherwise archive-specific manifests.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: only plates group images.\n0.6: Possible: scenes group spatially related images, but say nothing about other relations.\n0.9dev: Possible: not in 0.9dev; RFC-8 collections would cover it.

title: Viewer rendering state stored with a collection
statement: As a researcher sharing a multi-image view,\nI want to store the view state (position, rotation, per-layer colours, shaders, visibility) alongside the images, in viewer-specific containers,\nso that others open the same view.
workaround: Viewer-specific state files or URLs.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: omero rendering covers one image's channels only.\n0.6: Out of spec: same.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: not in 0.9dev; RFC-8 collections would cover it. RFC-8 gives containers, not a rendering spec.

title: Linking tables, meshes and other derived data to images
statement: As a bioimage analyst,\nI want to link derived data (tables, meshes, probability maps) in Zarr or other formats to an OME-Zarr image,\nso that tools can discover it without each defining its own sub-spec.
workaround: Tool-specific conventions, e.g. ngio tables (Fractal) or MoBIE label tables.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: only labels are defined.\n0.6: Out of spec: same.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: not in 0.9dev; RFC-8 collections would cover it.

title: Gallery and grid views
statement: As a researcher,\nI want to show many similar images (each possibly with its labels) as a grid of thumbnails from their lowest resolution,\nso that I get an overview and can zoom into the interesting ones.
workaround: Tool-specific tables, e.g. MoBIE collection tables, Zarrcade, BioFile Finder.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no gallery grouping; plates only for wells.\n0.6: Out of spec: scenes place images in space, not as a grid.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: not in 0.9dev; RFC-8 collections would cover it.
examples: https://github.com/normanrz/ngff-rfc8-collection-examples/ RFC-8 examples incl. OpenOrganelle mito gallery

title: View and analyse stitched data without a fused copy
statement: As a facility or analyst handling large tiled acquisitions,\nI want viewers and analysis libraries to fuse tiles on demand from the raw tiles and their registration transforms,\nso that I need not store a fused copy (roughly doubling storage) or pay to compute fusion for regions nobody looks at.
user_classes: Data manager; Bioimage analyst; Tool developer
workaround: Write the fused image anyway.
notes: 0.5: Possible: translation-only tiles as separate images in an implicit shared space.\n0.6: Core: a scene holds every tile and its transform to a shared space, which is all a reader needs to fuse; doing it fast for many tiles is STORY-073.\n0.9dev: Core: same.

title: Find which tiles cover a region
statement: As a viewer developer,\nI want a world-to-tile lookup (spatial index) for collections of thousands of tiles,\nso that rendering a region does not require reading every tile's metadata, one request per node, on remote storage.
workaround: Read all tile metadata up front, or a tool-specific index.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no index.\n0.6: Out of spec: readers must scan every transform in the scene.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: RFC-8 does not define one; its extensions could carry one, or consolidated metadata.

title: Provenance of registration and fusion
statement: As a researcher,\nI want a registration stored as its own result that references the raw tiles and records how it was produced (tool, parameters),\nso that I can reproduce or audit how a fused image was made.
workaround: Tool logs or custom attributes.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: nowhere to record it.\n0.6: Out of spec: a scene holds the transforms, but there is no provenance field.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: RFC-8 gives attributes and source references but no provenance schema.

title: Select a channel by name
statement: As a bioimage analyst running batch analysis on many multi-channel images,\nI want to look up a channel's index from a stable name (e.g. "nuclei"),\nso my pipeline finds the right channel even when channel order differs between datasets.
workaround: omero.channels[].label
notes:
0.5: Core extension: transitional omero.channels[].label names each channel, but labels are not required to be unique or stable identifiers.
0.6: Core extension: unchanged; omero still transitional.
0.9dev: Core extension: ome/ngff-spec#87 makes some omero fields optional; RFC-7 is expected to give channels proper identifiers.
Workarounds seen in the wild: omero.channels label, or even channel color, used as identifier. CF conventions handle this with a labels/auxiliary coordinate array along the axis (d-v-b).

title: High-content screening plate layout
statement: As a screening facility,\nI want to store a plate as wells and fields of view (with plate acquisitions), each field a multiscale image,\nso viewers and analysis tools can navigate and load sparse plates by well and field.
notes:
0.5: Core: plate/well metadata (HCS spec since 0.1.4).
0.6: Core: unchanged; acquisitions, rowIndex/columnIndex, field_count.
0.9dev: Core: unchanged.
Defined in the HCS spec (plate/well metadata) since 0.1-0.4; record of the original need.

title: Segmentations stored with the image
statement: As a bioimage analyst,\nI want to store one or more multiscale integer label images (segmentations) inside the image they segment,\nso viewers discover and overlay them without extra configuration.
notes:
0.5: Core: labels group with image-label multiscales (since 0.1.3).
0.6: Core: unchanged; labels can be linked with identity/scale/translation transforms.
0.9dev: Core: unchanged.
Basis of the labels spec since 0.1.

title: Downsampling factors of pyramid levels
statement: As a tool developer (e.g. BigDataViewer),\nI want each resolution level to declare how it was downsampled relative to the full resolution, including when only some axes (e.g. not z) are downsampled,\nso I do not have to infer factors from array shapes, which fails when extents are not divisible.
workaround: Divide per-level scale by level-0 scale
notes:
0.5: Possible: per-level scale transforms give the factors by division; multiscales type/metadata describe the method. No dedicated field.
0.6: Possible: same; spec now says scale MUST express the factor when no physical size applies.
0.9dev: Possible: unchanged.
Since 0.4 per-level scale transforms make this derivable; d-v-b argued tools should use grid spacing instead.

title: Volumes with millions of chunks on a file system
statement: As a user storing large volumes on local or network file systems,\nI want chunks laid out in nested directories rather than one flat folder,\nso the file system copes with millions of chunks.
notes:
0.5: Core: Zarr v3 chunk key encoding ("/" separator) nests chunks (since 0.2 for v2).
0.6: Core: unchanged.
0.9dev: Core: unchanged.
Addressed at Zarr level (dimension_separator, then Zarr v3 chunk key encoding).

title: Meshes stored with images
statement: As a bioimage analyst producing surface reconstructions,\nI want to store meshes (vertices, faces, properties) next to the images they come from,\nso meshes and images can be shared and viewed together.
workaround: Neuroglancer precomputed meshes or side files
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no mesh storage.
0.6: Out of spec: no mesh storage.
0.9dev: Out of spec: mesh RFC in draft (kephale).
Proposal based on PLY; glyg suggested GeoJSON for ROIs/points instead.

title: Vector shapes and annotations
statement: As a image annotator,\nI want to store polygons, polylines, lines, ellipses and points in image coordinates,\nso viewers like vizarr and napari can display and exchange my annotations.
workaround: GeoJSON side files
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no shapes.
0.6: Out of spec: no shapes.
0.9dev: Out of spec: no shapes.
GeoJSON vs WKT discussed; neither has ellipses/rectangles or nD.

title: Regions of interest
statement: As a analyst processing fields of view or organoids within a large dataset,\nI want to define regions of interest (e.g. bounding boxes in physical units) on an image,\nso processing and viewing can target those regions without copying data.
workaround: ROI tables (Fractal) or separate cropped images
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no ROI or table spec.
0.6: Out of spec: a crop can be stored as its own image placed with a translation in a scene, but a region without copying data has no place.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
Options: ROI tables (Fractal; preferred by bogovicj) vs crops in transformations (MoBIE).

title: Units and meaning of image values
statement: As a scientist storing quantitative images (FLIM lifetimes, calcium dF/F, AFM height),\nI want to record the physical unit and kind (continuous, categorical) of the stored values, even per channel,\nso the values can be interpreted and processed correctly.
workaround: Custom attributes; Zarr unit convention (zarr-convention-uom)
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: units only for axes, not for values.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
#37 asks about channels whose values have different units (compound datasets). Zarr convention for units: clbarnes/zarr-convention-uom.

title: Interoperability with xarray and CF conventions
statement: As a developer working across geoscience and bioimaging tools,\nI want OME-Zarr images to be readable as xarray datasets with explicit coordinates and CF-style metadata,\nso domain-agnostic tools can use bioimages and we reuse mature conventions.
notes: 0.5: Possible: Zarr v3 dimension_names (MUST since 0.5.2) lets xarray open each array with named dims, but without coordinates or CF attributes.\n0.6: Possible: same; coordinates transforms give explicit per-sample coordinates, but as multiscale groups xarray does not read.\n0.9dev: Unsure: RFC-3 lifts axis restrictions, closer to xarray; no CF mapping defined.

title: Per-label names and display properties
statement: As a medical/bioimage tool developer (e.g. 3D Slicer),\nI want each label value to carry a name, standard term, color, opacity and custom properties in one consistent structure,\nso others can tell what each labeled object represents.
notes:
0.5: Core: image-label colors (rgba) and properties with arbitrary keys per label-value.
0.6: Core: unchanged.
0.9dev: Core: unchanged; colors/properties split (ngff#79) still open; labels RFC expected.
#164: user cannot tell what IDR labels represent when names are missing.

title: Pixel origin at center or corner
statement: As a developer exchanging images between 2D and 3D tools (ITK, VTK, napari),\nI want the spec to define whether coordinates refer to pixel centers or corners,\nso images and annotations align across tools without half-pixel shifts.
notes:
0.5: Unsure: check whether the 0.5 text defines the pixel origin; the explicit "Coordinate convention" section came with RFC-5.
0.6: Core: "The pixel/voxel center is the origin of the continuous coordinate system"; pixel = half-open box [-0.5, 0.5).
0.9dev: Core: unchanged.
Pixel-center convention adopted; #492 asks to define "pixel" consistently.

title: Fast plate overview
statement: As a viewer developer (vizarr, napari),\nI want a precomputed low-resolution overview of a whole plate,\nso opening a 384-well plate does not take thousands of requests.
workaround: Viewers load the lowest level of every well
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no plate-level preview.\n0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.

title: Millions of spots from spatial omics
statement: As a spatial-omics analyst,\nI want to store millions of detected spots (2D/3D coordinates, gene name, quality) with the image,\nso they can be loaded chunk-wise, locally or from object storage.
workaround: Parquet / AnnData (SpatialData) next to the image
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no points or tables.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
d-v-b: zarr arrays are a poor fit for tables; consider parquet etc.

title: Single-resolution images
statement: As a analyst extracting a small region from one scale level,\nI want to save a single-resolution image with axes and transforms without multiscale boilerplate,\nso small derived images stay simple yet valid.
workaround: Multiscales with one dataset
notes:
0.5: Possible: a multiscales group with one level is valid, if verbose.
0.6: Possible: same; one level still needs coordinateSystems and a transform.
0.9dev: Possible: unchanged; RFC-8 proposes a singlescale node.
RFC-8 proposes a singlescale node.

title: Description, license and authorship
statement: As a data producer sharing an image,\nI want to store a free-text description, license, authors and contributions with the image,\nso reuse terms and credit travel with the data.
workaround: Custom attributes; OME-XML via bioformats2raw for some fields
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no description, license or author fields.\n0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.

title: Sparse arrays
statement: As a user of mask images or mass spectrometry imaging with thousands of channels,\nI want to store mostly-empty data as sparse arrays,\nso storage and computation scale with content, not volume.
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: dense arrays only; needs Zarr-level sparse support (zarr-specs#245).
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
Maintainers point to Zarr-level support (zarr-specs#245).

title: Several image types per HCS field of view
statement: As a developer of an optical pooled screening pipeline,\nI want each field of view in a plate to hold the raw image, float derived images and segmentations together,\nso co-registered outputs with different dtypes stay organized in the HCS layout.
workaround: Sibling plates for derived images; labels for integer masks
notes:
0.5: Awkward: well images must be multiscales images; float derived images fit only as separate plates or extra fields of view.
0.6: Awkward: a scene can group co-registered images, but a well field must be a multiscales image, so scenes cannot sit in wells (ngff#476).
0.9dev: Awkward: unchanged.
#476 proposes nesting scenes in HCS.

title: Unique identifiers for images
statement: As a curator cataloguing many OME-Zarr datasets,\nI want each image to carry a stable unique identifier,\nso copies and derived versions can be tracked across stores.
workaround: Custom attributes
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no identifier field.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
Problem statement still debated (d-v-b, mkitti).
